subject.title: [Bug]: Block streaming can drop paragraph separators across streamed updates

question: Should the permanent fix use in-band separator preservation in one linked PR, or should the streaming pipeline first carry explicit boundary metadata for paragraph/newline/hard split seams?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the durable boundary contract affects shared streamed delivery semantics and two open PRs already propose the narrower text-based fix shape.

options.title: Consolidate one separator-preserving PR
options.body: Review one linked PR as the canonical fix, require chunker reconstruction and coalescer no-double-separator coverage, and close the other PR as superseded after choosing the viable path.

options.title: Require boundary metadata first
options.body: Pause the linked text-based PRs until a metadata-carrying separator contract is designed and tested through chunking, coalescing, and delivery.

options.title: Keep issue open for redesign
options.body: Reject the current text-only direction and leave this issue open for a maintainer-sponsored redesign of streaming boundary semantics.

recommendation.title: Consolidate one separator-preserving PR
recommendation.body: Review one linked PR as the canonical fix, require chunker reconstruction and coalescer no-double-separator coverage, and close the other PR as superseded after choosing the viable path.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and later refined the paragraph/newline block-streaming behavior now at the center of the boundary contract choice.
